doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Riverside and the New York scene
title: Fireside gigs, Herbie Nichols and joining Monk at the Five Spot
summary: Ware plays weekends on the Bowery with Dave Amram, Ray Bryant and Herbie Nichols, then joins Monk with Trane at the Five Spot and records Mulligan Meets Monk.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Things kind of slowed up, and I worked a couple of gigs down at the Fire Spot Fireside and Dave Amram Amarand had a weekend down there with me, and I was in the rhythm section, and it was just a little hamburger joint on the Bowery there; we were

trying to make a little club out of it, and the next weekend, Ray Bryant came in on piano, and the following weekend, Herbie Nichols -- I was able to play with him; he was a genius. Beautiful young man -- not too long before he died. And then Thelonious said, "Come on down," and we with Trane and Shadow went down there, and we played -- and that was the gig. I stayed with that gig, plus recordings, first record it, still at Riverside now, and one night we had a recording date with Gerry Mulligan and Monk, called Mulligan Meets Monk. And we got through with the date and I rushed down to the club from and the recording date, and I hadn't eaten, so I put my fiddle on the bandstand, and I said I was going to go around the corner to get a sandwich; I'll be right back."
